messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm) water freezes at roughly **–2.5 °C**.  

**Why?**  
Water expands when it freezes, so the solid phase has a larger molar volume than the liquid. According to the Clausius–Clapeyron relation, this means that the freezing point drops as the external pressure is lowered. The phase diagram of water shows that at 10 kPa the solid–liquid equilibrium temperature is about –2.5 °C (the exact value depends slightly on the reference data set, but it’s in the –2 °C to –3 °C range).
